subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit per-agent delegate-only/self-deny tool policy, and what public config shape should own that security boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this changes how tool authority crosses agent boundaries and adds public config surface, so automation should not choose the permanent semantics or name.

options.title: Approve delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides tools from the requester's model while preserving normal deny-wins semantics for child inheritance.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy
options.body: Let per-spawn child narrowing land first and defer parent direct-use prevention to a later unified tool-policy design.

options.title: Reject escalation by design
options.body: Keep tool policy strictly monotonic and document separate agent profiles as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides tools from the requester's model while preserving normal deny-wins semantics for child inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest prior-review routing signal for the public API and security-boundary choice.
